_comment: What Phase A was measured with. scripts/reproduce_phase_a.sh reads this file rather than
carrying the values itself, so a rerun and this record cannot drift apart.
The repository commit is deliberately absent: this file lives inside the repository, so a
commit written here would describe the state before itself. `repo_tag` closes that without
circularity -- this file names a tag, and the tag is created afterwards pointing at the
commit that contains this file. Without it a rerun a year from now uses a year-old lock
against whatever the harness has become, which is not the thing that produced phase_a.json.
gpu: NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3090, 24576 MiB, compute capability 8.6
_repo_tag_note: Create as an annotated, signed tag on the commit that carries this file: `git tag -s phase-a-v1 -m 'Phase A as measured'`. The reproduce script warns when HEAD is not at it, because a warning is honest about a tag that may not exist yet and a hard failure would block the script in the repository it ships in.

toolchain._source: llamacpp-*/build/CMakeCache.txt and CMakeFiles/*/CMake*Compiler.cmake, read 2026-08-27. These are the settings the measured binaries were configured with, recovered from the trees themselves; no contemporaneous toolchain record was kept, so this is evidence rather than a log.

_toolchain_note: A mismatch here does not invalidate a reproduction; it bounds how far the two builds can be assumed identical. The script reports differences and continues, except for CUDA, which it already pins hard.

dflash2_archive._why: dflash2_source points at pull/27342/head, a live ref. That PR's head has already moved past the measured commit, and a force-push or a deleted branch can make the object unreachable, at which point this lock names a commit nobody can fetch.
dflash2_archive._prerequisite_note: verified to be an ancestor of llama_master_commit, so a clone checked out at the pinned master can always complete the bundle. `git bundle verify` passes; scripts/reproduce_phase_a.sh prefers it over the live PR ref and falls back to the ref only if the object is missing.
dflash2_archive._swhid_note: swh:1:rev:d1a522fc89c96d1a3057e35681f0c4859810623c once archive.softwareheritage.org has visited ggml-org/llama.cpp with that commit reachable. SWHIDs are ISO/IEC 18670 and derived from content, so the identifier is already fixed by the commit; archival is what makes it retrievable if GitHub ever stops serving it.
